ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are upper and lower common wires forming two common nodes; the left branch is a current source labeled 3 A with the arrow downward, the middle branch is a 3 Ω resistor, and the right branch is a 12 V voltage source, with the label showing the upper terminal as + and the lower terminal as −. The top wire is labeled with current I, and the arrow direction is to the left, that is, flowing from the top terminal of the voltage source on the right along the upper wire to the left side. Reasoning: The 12 V voltage source on the right fixes the upper node potential as 12 V higher than the lower node, so the two ends of the middle 3 Ω resistor are also 12 V with upper positive and lower negative. The resistor current is 12 V / 3 Ω = 4 A, with direction from top to bottom. The left current source already has 3 A flowing from top to bottom. Writing KCL for the upper node, the currents leaving the upper node downward total 4 A + 3 A = 7 A, therefore the current I provided from the right side along the top wire to the left must be 7 A.

raw_record.question_text: In the DC circuit shown in the figure, what is the current \(I\)?

method.method_draft: First identify from the image that the 12 V source, 3 Ω resistor, and 3 A downward current source are connected in parallel between a common top and bottom node. Since the voltage source has + at the top, the resistor has 12 V from top to bottom, giving 4 A downward through the 3 Ω resistor. At the top node, 3 A leaves downward through the current source and 4 A leaves downward through the resistor, so by KCL the current supplied along the top wire from the right branch is 7 A in the indicated leftward direction. Therefore I = 7 A.

method.method_draft: View the right 12 V source as feeding the rest of the circuit. The load connected across it consists of the middle 3 Ω resistor and the left current source, both between the same top and bottom rails. Because the 12 V source fixes the load voltage, the resistor draws 4 A from the top rail to the bottom rail. The current source also draws 3 A from top to bottom as indicated. Thus the total current that must enter the load from the source along the upper rail is 4 A + 3 A = 7 A, matching the arrow direction for I. Therefore I = 7 A.
